hints: Look carefully at Fig. 6.1 - P points to the folded inner membranes, Q points to the fluid-filled interior. Which stage of respiration needs a membrane and which needs a fluid space?
Recall where the Krebs cycle enzymes are dissolved and where the electron transport chain plus ATP synthase must be embedded to pump protons.
Link each compound to its cycle - acetyl CoA enters and oxaloacetate is regenerated in the Krebs cycle, while ATP synthase and phospholipid bilayer belong to the membrane system.
walkthrough:
Identify P and Q from the micrograph**
P points to the cristae, which are folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane. Q points to the matrix, the aqueous interior enclosed by the inner membrane. So P = membrane location, Q = matrix location.

Place the membrane proteins**
Oxidative phosphorylation needs the electron transport chain and ATP synthase embedded in the inner membrane to create and use a proton gradient. A phospholipid bilayer is the membrane itself. Both therefore locate to P.

Place the Krebs cycle intermediates**
The link reaction produces acetyl CoA which diffuses into the matrix, where it combines with oxaloacetate to start the Krebs cycle. All Krebs enzymes and intermediates are in the matrix fluid. Both therefore locate to Q.
Final answer: ATP synthase - P; acetyl CoA - Q; phospholipid bilayer - P; oxaloacetate - Q

hints: Check how the last column was obtained for the other cells - divide mean number per cell by mean cell volume and keep the $\times 10^{-3}$ format.
walkthrough:
Apply number divided by volume**
Mean number per $\mu m^3$ = $\frac{\text{mean number per cell}}{\text{mean cell volume}} = \frac{2000}{125000} = 0.016$. Written to match the table this is $16.00 \times 10^{-3}$ per $\mu m^3$.

hints: Start from the function of mitochondria - what useful product do they supply, and compare the heart value $44.44 \times 10^{-3}$ with the fat value $0.17 \times 10^{-3}$ per $\mu m^3$.
Think about what heart muscle does continuously compared with fat storage tissue, and what that means for ATP demand.
walkthrough:
Link mitochondria to ATP supply**
Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, producing ATP. A higher density of mitochondria per $\mu m^3$ means a greater capacity to supply ATP.

Compare energy demands**
Heart cells contract continuously to pump blood and so have a very high, constant demand for ATP for muscle contraction. Fat cells are mainly storage and are relatively inactive with low ATP demand. This explains $44.44 \times 10^{-3}$ versus $0.17 \times 10^{-3}$ per $\mu m^3$.
Final answer: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration to produce ATP; heart / cardiac muscle cells are more active, contract continuously and so need more ATP / energy than fat cells.

hints: If two cells both have 2000 mitochondria, could those mitochondria still be different in a way that affects how much respiration they can do?
walkthrough:
Why count alone misleads**
Aerobic capacity depends not just on how many mitochondria are present but on how large each one is and how much inner membrane with electron transport proteins it contains. A large mitochondrion with dense cristae can respire much faster than a small one, so mean number per cell alone cannot be used to compare ability to respire aerobically.
Final answer: Mitochondria vary in size / volume and in surface area of inner membrane / cristae, so number alone does not indicate total respiratory capacity.
